label: First copy step after <DEL> (outputting orig[1]) in long sequences, boosted when orig[1]/orig[2] is q/e/w/y/0/n
explanation: Fires only at the step right after the first copied output (t = L+1, recall_idx == 1, input = orig[0], output = orig[1]); 100% of activations are there, and it never fires in the original or delimiter phases or at any later copy step. Within that slot it fires on about 10% of sequences overall. Firing rate rises sharply with length: 0 for L<=4, rare at L=5-6, about 25% at L=9 (L>=7 covers 95% of firings, 96% of mass). Rate and magnitude also depend strongly on the identity of the token being output (orig[1]) and the next one (orig[2]): q, e, w, y, 0, n give 4-7x lift, and the top activations (up to 5.1) are L>=8 sequences where both orig[1] and orig[2] are in {q,e,w,y}. Input token, first token, digit count and repeats barely matter. The firing condition looks like a graded combination of length and these output identities rather than a crisp rule: on dev, the predicate gets precision 0.45, recall 0.78, mass recall 0.88. The low-activation misses are long sequences whose orig[1]/orig[2] are other letters.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the next token to output (most: q, w, e, y, n, 0; least: r, 3, p, i) and the token being output (most: q, e, w, y, 0, n; least: 3, r, p, i); timing cues that raise it most: recall_idx=1, L=9 & t=10, L=8 & t=9.
